A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the local muon density spectra are sensitive to the hadronic interaction model and can be used for a more detailed study of the high energy cosmic ray composition.

the local muon density spectra obtained with the DECOR detector at large zenith angles are in good agreement with predictions for all hadronic interaction models considered, except for the case of the QGSJET-II-04 model, which significantly overestimates the number of muon bundles at small zenith angles.
the muon bundles observed by DECOR at large zenith angles are a unique probe for high-energy hadronic models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the observed intensity of the events at the local muon density 1–3 is higher than expectations by a factor of 2–4.

the observed excess of muon bundles at the horizon is not a result of an excess of primary cosmic rays at 10 18 – 10 19 eV but a result of the excess of muons in hadronic cascades at large zenith angles.

the muon density at large zenith angles is not a good tool to discriminate among hadronic interaction models at energies around the ankle, but it is sensitive to the high-energy tail of the cosmic ray spectrum.
